description: Track medieval merchants, a city-devouring fire and a soaring Norman landmark through Norwich's old streets.
short_description: Hunt carved dragons and crooked lanes before reaching Norwich's oldest recorded alehouse.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
recommended_age: Recommended 10+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A central walking route on public streets and historic precinct paths, with no building entry required.

before_you_go.terrain: A central walking route on public streets and historic precinct paths. Every clue can be solved without entering a building.
before_you_go.steps: No required steps are known, though temporary diversions may vary.
before_you_go.accessibility: Public pavements and paths throughout; check current diversions if step-free access is essential.
before_you_go.toilets: Check local public facilities before setting off; customer toilets may depend on opening hours.
before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable walking shoes should be suitable.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the finishing venue’s current dog policy before entering.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally possible on public paths; check temporary diversions and busy crossings.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find a merchant's hall where fifteen timber beasts once watched cargo arrive from across the sea.
stops.Hint_1: Begin on King Street, close to the River Wensum.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the medieval trading hall now occupied by the National Centre for Writing.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Merchant Robert Toppes built Dragon Hall in about 1427 to display, store and sell goods from Norfolk and Europe. Its great trading room used more than 500 oak timbers and was decorated with fifteen carved dragons, giving the restored building its modern name.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find a crooked hill rebuilt after flames ate nearly every house but one.
stops.Hint_1: Head north-west towards the Norwich Lanes and cross the river.
stops.Hint_2: Search for the cobbled street of leaning timber-framed buildings near Princes Street.
stops.Unlock_Fact: A major fire swept through Elm Hill in 1507 and destroyed most of the street. The Britons Arms is traditionally identified as the only surviving building from before the blaze; the picturesque houses around it were rebuilt during the Tudor period and later centuries.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Pass through a gate to find a Norman giant wearing a stone spire and watched by peregrines.
stops.Hint_1: Walk east into the Cathedral Close.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the vast pale-stone cathedral with a spire rising above the city.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Construction of Norwich Cathedral began in 1096 under Bishop Herbert de Losinga. Its Norman nave remains remarkably complete, while the 96-metre stone spire is the second tallest cathedral spire in England. Peregrine falcons have also nested high on the building.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Leave the Close to find the first couple sharing Norwich's oldest recorded pint.
stops.Hint_1: Continue north-east towards Bishopgate and the river.
stops.Hint_2: Find the small flint-walled pub at number 17 named after the biblical pair.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! The Adam and Eve is traditionally called Norwich's oldest pub, with its earliest known written reference dating to 1249. The present building has changed over the centuries, but the tiny rooms still provide an atmospheric finish for food, a pint or a soft drink.
